$comment: Single source of truth for Style Kit component props. The Python pipeline validates every scene spec against these schemas; the prompt shows them to Claude. Logical canvas is 1280x720, origin top-left. Colors are token names: ink, inkSoft, muted, accent, indigo, sage, ochre (or #hex).

common.at: seconds from scene start when the entrance begins
common.until: optional seconds when it fades out (0.35s); omit to stay to the end
common.motion: Any element may also take `motion`: [{cue|at, dx, dy | x, y, scale, rotate, opacity, dur}] to move/scale/turn it (each key starts a smooth move lasting dur, default 1.2 s; x/y = new centre), and `loop`: bob|float|pulse|breathe|spin|sway|shake for an idle animation after its entrance (`loopSpeed` scales it). Any element may also take `depth` (-1 far … 0 the subject … 1 near): it sets parallax when the camera moves and which plane depth of field blurs (Landscape defaults to -0.7, Guide to 0.35).

TitleCard.description: Full-width opening title, hand-written, with a vermilion brush underline. Use once, at the start of a lesson's first scene. Fade it out (until) before other content appears.

Heading.description: Top-of-frame heading (default x=64, y=44) with short accent underline. One per idea/shot.

Text.description: A short hand-written label or sentence, written on left-to-right. (x,y) is the TOP-LEFT of the block for align=left, top-center for center. Wraps at maxWidth; auto-shrinks to fit maxLines.

EquationWrite.description: A formula written stroke-by-stroke in the serif/math face. Use plain Unicode maths (² ³ √ π Σ μ σ Δ ≈ ≠ ≤ ≥ ± × ÷ − → x̄ ½). No LaTeX, no subscript letters (write x_i as 'xi' or avoid).

BulletReveal.description: A list of 2–5 short points, each revealed with a dot. Give `times` (absolute scene seconds, one per item) to land each bullet on the narration word that introduces it.

Callout.description: A sticky note (default top-right, w=380) for the key idea, a definition, or a 'watch out'. (x,y) is its top-left.

Counter.description: A number that counts from `from` to `to` (big serif figure). (x,y) is top-center by default.

Table.description: A small table (≤5 rows × ≤4 cols), first row is the header. Rows appear one by one.

Underline.description: Hand-drawn accent underline under a `target` element (or explicit x,y,w box). Use on the narration word that stresses it.

CircleHighlight.description: Hand-drawn ellipse around a `target` element (or explicit x,y,w,h box).

MarkerHighlight.description: Translucent highlighter swipe behind a `target` element (or box).

Arrow.description: Curved hand-drawn arrow. `from`/`to` are element ids (snaps to their edges) or [x,y] points. Optional small label at the midpoint.

Box.description: A sketchy rectangle with a centered label. (x,y) is top-left.

Flow.description: A diagram of 2–6 labelled nodes joined by arrows; nodes appear first, then edges. Node (x,y) is its CENTER; default node size 210x92. Keep ≥ 260px between node centers horizontally.

AxesPlot.description: Axes with ticks plus 1–3 series drawn progressively. A series is either `fn` (expression in x: + - * / ^, sin cos tan exp log sqrt abs, pi, e; e.g. "x^2/4", "sin(x)") or `points` [[x,y],...]. kind: line | points | bars. (x,y,w,h) is the plot area.

NumberLine.description: A horizontal number line with ticks and labelled marks that pop in (optionally each at absolute time `at`).

BarChart.description: 2–8 labelled bars growing from a baseline. (x,y,w,h) is the bar area; labels sit below.

SideBySide.description: Two-column comparison (titles + up to 4 bullets each) with a divider; fills the frame below the heading.

ProgressBar.description: Thin lesson-progress bar at the very bottom (value 0..1, animates from `from`). Usually added automatically.

RecapCard.description: Full-frame 'back to the lesson' card. Used automatically for resume recaps.

FrozenFrame.description: ANSWER CLIPS ONLY. Re-renders the paused lesson scene at time t as the backdrop, holds it, then dims it (and optionally zooms toward cx,cy) so annotations can grow out of it. The pipeline fills `spec` itself — never write it.

Prop.description: One illustration from the library, with a gentle built-in idle animation (sun rays turn, waves roll, heart beats, gears spin). (x,y) is its CENTRE; size = height in px (default 160). Other elements can target its anchors as "id.anchor" (every prop has center/top/bottom/left/right plus its own, see the catalog). `state` 0–1 drives fill levels, growth or glow; `stateKeys` animate it. `talk` moves its mouth with the narration (Storybook faces).

Particles.description: A continuous stream of small things moving along a path: evaporating vapour, falling rain, blood cells, electrons, nutrients, light. `path` points are [x,y], "elementId" or "elementId.anchor" (2 points + optional `curve`, or up to 12 points for a smooth route). `spread` widens the stream sideways (e.g. rain 60–90); `speed` px/s. Kinds: dot, drop, vapor, bubble, snow, spark, arrow, rbc, wbc, water, molecule, oxygen, co2, glucose, salt, urea, ion, electron, photon, heat, leaf, nutrient, or any prop kind (drawn small).

Tube.description: A vessel, pipe, tubule, root or river drawn along a path (it draws itself in), optionally with things flowing inside (`flow`). Anchors: start, q1, middle, q3, end.

Journey.description: One character or object travelling along a path over `travel` seconds (or looping): a raindrop's trip through the cycle, food through the gut, a red blood cell round the body. Optional dotted `trail`.

Label.description: A short label at (x,y) (text centre) with a leader line and dot pointing at `target` ("id", "id.anchor" or [x,y]). The way to name parts of an illustration. Keep labels clear of the drawing.

Guide.description: Buddy, the friendly guide character for young learners: (x,y) = centre, size = height (default 190). Talks (mouth moves) while the narration plays, blinks, and looks at what it points to. pose: idle | wave | point | think | cheer; change it over time with `poses`. Storybook kit only. Its design follows the kit (Buddy, a block figure, a chalk stick figure); `pointAt` lands the hand on the target.

Landscape.description: A full-frame living landscape (sky, sun, land, sea with rolling waves, mountains, a flowing river, trees) that builds itself in. Put it first. Anchors: sky, sun, sea, seaSurface, land, ground, mountain, mountainSide, river, riverMouth, cloud, cloudLeft, cloudRight. Horizon (default 470) is where land meets sky.

Nephron.description: An accurate schematic nephron (≈620×540 px at scale 1, centred at x,y): afferent/efferent arterioles, glomerulus in Bowman's capsule, proximal tubule, loop of Henle (descending/ascending limbs), distal tubule, collecting duct, peritubular capillaries, cortex/medulla zones. `flows` switch on animated processes at given times: blood, filtrate (filtration), reabsorb (glucose/salt/water back to blood), secrete, urine. `highlight` dims everything else. Anchors: glomerulus, capsule, pct, descending, loop, ascending, dct, duct, ductEnd, afferent, efferent, capillary, cortex, medulla.

Body.description: A human figure with organs inside (centre x,y; size = height, default 560): brain, lungs, heart, liver, stomach, kidneys, intestines, bladder. Show a subset with `organs`, emphasise with `highlight`, name them with `labels`. Anchors: each organ name, kidneyLeft, kidneyRight, head, chest, belly.

Epithelium.description: Cell-level transport across an epithelium (kidney tubule, gut, glands): lumen on the left, 1–3 epithelial cells (apical brush border, nucleus, mitochondria, tight junctions) in the middle, interstitium and a capillary with flowing red cells on the right. Each item of `transporters` appears at its cue on the apical or basolateral membrane (`pos` 0–1 = height) and moves its `carries` through it: ion names ("Na+", "K+", "Cl−", "H+", "Ca2+", "HCO3−") or particle kinds (glucose, water, urea, AA). Cargo moves toward the blood unless toward="lumen"; an exchanger's and a pump's second cargo moves the opposite way (3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in). `paracellular` sends water or ions between the cells. Default box 1080×430 centred at (640,405). Anchors: lumen, cell, nucleus, apical, basolateral, junction, interstitium, blood, transporter0…

Synapse.description: SET. A chemical synapse, accurate and alive (≈900×620 at scale 1, centred at x,y; the axon enters from the top). Stages (each on the word that names it; they accumulate): spike (an action potential arrives down the axon), calcium (Ca²+ channels open, calcium flows in), release (vesicles dock and fuse, transmitter spills into the cleft), bind (transmitter crosses and binds; receptors open), flow (ions rush into the postsynaptic cell, which depolarises), reuptake (transmitter is taken back up; receptors close). `labels` name parts on cue; `highlight` one part. Anchors: axon, terminal, vesicle, vesicles, mitochondrion, channel, channelRight, cleft, transmitter, receptor, receptors, postsynaptic, membrane.

Cell.description: SET. A eukaryotic (animal) cell filling most of the frame (≈980×600 at its default scale 0.85): membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus with envelope, pores and nucleolus, rough ER with ribosomes, Golgi, mitochondria with cristae, a lysosome. Stages: transcribe (mRNA copied in the nucleus leaves through a pore), translate (a ribosome builds a protein bead by bead), ship (a vesicle carries it ER → Golgi → membrane and releases it outside), power (mitochondria give off ATP sparks). Anchors: nucleus, nucleolus, pore, er, ribosome, golgi, mitochondrion, lysosome, membrane, cytoplasm, vesicle.

Molecule.description: SET. One molecule in ball-and-stick (or `style` space-filling), atoms in teaching colours with their letters (≈170×130 at its default scale 1.8). Stages: vibrate (bonds stretch, as when heated), split (bonds break, atoms drift apart), spin. Anchors: center, atom0, atom1…

Reaction.description: SET. A chemical reaction you can watch: reactant molecules on the left, an arrow, products on the right (≈900×300 at its default scale 1.35); on `react` their bonds break, the very same atoms fly to their places in the products and new bonds form. The balanced equation is written beneath (counted from the lists, so list each molecule as many times as it occurs). Stages: shake (reactants jiggle, energy rising), react. Anchors: reactants, products, arrow, equation.

Orbits.description: SET. A star (or planet) with bodies circling it on tilted orbits seen a little from above: bodies pass behind and in front, trail a fading arc, are lit on the side facing the centre, and can count their laps (`counters`) to race a day against a year or one planet against another. `period` is film-seconds per orbit (relative speeds matter, not real ones). Stages: start (bodies set off; otherwise they move from the entrance), stop. Bodies keep moving, so frame them with shots on the set itself, never close on one body. Anchors: center, each body's name (where it starts), <name>Orbit.

Machine.description: SET. A mechanism that really works (≈900×460). `preset`: gears (a meshing train from `teeth`, e.g. [24,12,36]; each gear turns the other way at the ratio of its teeth), crank (a crankshaft driving a piston in a cylinder; stage combust adds the flame), lever (a beam on a fulcrum at `fulcrum` −1..1; stage push lifts the load, release lets it down), pulley (stage pull raises the load). Stages: start, fast, stop, push, release, pull, combust. Labels parts: driver, driven, wheel, rod, piston, cylinder, fulcrum, effort, load, pulley. Anchors: driver, driven, gear0…, and the label parts.

Circuit.description: SET. A simple circuit loop (≈760×420): the wires draw on, then `parts` sit on it (battery left, switch top, bulb right, resistor bottom, motor). Stage close: the switch closes, electrons drift round, the bulb lights; open: it stops. Anchors: battery, switch, bulb, resistor, wire, current.

Timeline.description: SET. Years to scale along a band (`start`, `end`; negative years are BCE), with `eras` as soft bands and `events` that pop up on cue (alternating above and below); a gold line draws on to the latest event. `length` may exceed the frame (up to 4000): the camera can travel along it with shots on events. Anchors: start, end, center, e0, e1… (events in order).

WorldMap.description: SET. The real world map (Natural Earth shapes) or a region of it: `view` world | europe | asia | africa | americas | north america | south america | india | south asia | middle east | east asia | oceania | mediterranean, or [lon0, lat0, lon1, lat1]. `regions` light up countries by name on cue; `flood` spreads a colour country by country outward from a place (an empire, a language, a disease); `routes` draw on between places with a traveller; `pins` drop on places. Places are country names or major cities (London, Rome, Delhi, Beijing, Cairo, Karakorum, Samarkand, Baghdad, Constantinople…). Anchors: each place you name (spaces removed, e.g. "map.NewYork"), center.

TokenGrid.description: SET. A crowd of `n` tokens (person figures, dots, or any prop kind: coin, house, drop, cell…) in a grid that pops in; `groups` recolour runs of them on cue ("1 in 4", "a third"), with a label above each group; `highlight` makes one token light up and pulse. Anchors: center, first, last, g0, g1… (group centres), highlight.

Bars.description: SET. Bars that grow to their values with counters ticking up, labels beside them (horizontal by default). `race`: all bars grow together at the same rate over `raceDur`, so the viewer watches who wins. Anchors: center, b0, b1…

Stamp.description: A claim stamped onto the frame (slams in, slightly tilted, with a double border and patchy ink); `strikeAt` (or a cue) draws a line through it: the reversal beat ("case closed? Not quite").

Contraption.description: SET. A whimsical machine that acts out an abstract process (≈860×480): `input` props drop into the hopper, the machine works (gears behind its window, a shudder, steam, a gauge that climbs) and `output` props come out of the chute and pile up (`grow`: each bigger than the last, for growth). Stages: feed (items go in every `every` seconds, `count` of them), stop. Labels parts: input, machine, output, gauge (their text comes from inputLabel, label, outputLabel, gaugeLabel). Anchors: hopper, input, machine, output, tray, gauge, crank.

Transition.description: A transition between two sets inside a scene: a cover that is full at its midpoint, where the old elements end and the new ones begin (end the old ones and start the new ones on the same cue as the Transition; the pipeline aligns them). `kind` defaults to the kit's signature (brush, iris, slide, bleed, glow, dissolve, eraser, sheet, print); `center` (an id or anchor) is where an iris closes or a bloom starts. Use at most one or two per scene, only when the place changes.
